formulations.Polymer system Notes: Comparison of high-purity anionically-polymerized PEO (HP-PEO, Mw≈1×10^6, ~1 ppm initiator residue, narrower PDI, no detectable low-MW fraction) vs commercial PEO (C-PEO, Aldrich, Mw≈900 kDa) as LiCF3SO3 electrolytes, O/Li=4–100 (salt wt fraction x=0.02–0.48), 65–125°C. PEO–LiCF3SO3 is two-phase (crystalline+amorphous) for 0.18<x<0.45 and single-phase amorphous below that (T>65°C). C-PEO shows an anomalous double-hump conductivity-vs-x curve at low salt content (O/Li>30), attributed to catalytic/ionic impurities; HP-PEO shows a smooth single maximum.
formulations.Arrhenius notes: Apparent activation energy at T=65°C, read from Fig.2 (circle=C-PEO) at O/Li=100 (x≈0.04). Conductivity at 85/125°C from Fig.1 digitized table nearest point x=0.03 (first conductivity maximum, small 0.01 offset). Fig.1 table values assigned to C-PEO (solid curve) based on the double-hump shape matching text's description of anomalous low-concentration behavior; HP-PEO (dashed) curve is smooth/single-maxima and not separately tabulated.
formulations.Notes: Tg/Tm not given numerically in this paper; text states thermal transitions equivalent to previously reported PEO-LiX phase diagrams (refs 9,10).
formulations.Reference: Fauteux, D.; Prud'homme, J.; Harvey, P.E. Solid State Ionics 1988, 28-30, 923-928.

formulations.Polymer system Notes: HP-PEO–LiClO4: interphase (passivation) resistance at the Li0/electrolyte interface (Fig.6, T=112°C) increases strongly with LiClO4 wt fraction (~12 Ω at x=0.02 up to ~400-410 Ω at x=0.16-0.22), unlike the roughly constant resistance seen for HP-PEO-LiCF3SO3. Activation energy of this interphase resistance varies from ~0.9 to ~0.65 eV with concentration (text, Section 3.2). Diffusion-limiting current for Li0/HP-PEO-LiClO4 at 70°C is ~1.5-2.0 mA/cm2 (Fig.8).

formulations.Polymer system Notes: PEO-LiAsF6 appears only in Fig.5, a plot of molar/specific conductance Λ (Ω^-1 mol^-1 cm^2) vs. C^1/2 (mol cm^-3)^1/2 at T=105°C, shown alongside PEO-LiCF3SO3, PEO-LiClO4, HP-PEO-LiCF3SO3 and HP-PEO-LiClO4 curves to qualitatively illustrate ion-association effects (Walden-type plot). LiAsF6 shows the steepest, most nearly linear decline of Λ with C^1/2 among the salts tested (from ~9.5 near C^1/2=1 down to ~0.5 by C^1/2=5), interpreted as indicating strong ion-pairing/association at low dilution relative to the other anions, which show broader maxima.
formulations.Polymer: C-PEO (commercial PEO, Aldrich; polymer purity/grade not specified for the LiAsF6 series, presumed C-PEO as for LiCF3SO3/LiClO4 series)
formulations.drying temp: 45-50 (polymer); 100-110 (salt, presumed same procedure as other LiX salts)
formulations.Notes: No conductivity (S/cm), Ea, Tg/Tm, or specific salt wt%/O:Li values are given anywhere in the text for the PEO-LiAsF6 system; it is only shown as one curve in Fig.5 in molar-conductance units (Ω^-1 mol^-1 cm^2), which is not directly convertible to bulk ionic conductivity (S/cm) without independently known concentrations at each point, and reading precise numeric values off this overlapping multi-curve plot was judged too uncertain to report. Field values left null accordingly; see Polymer system Notes for qualitative description.
formulations.Reference: Fauteux, D.; Prud'homme, J.; Harvey, P.E. Solid State Ionics 1988, 28-30, 923-928.
